cards.text: A long prayer to the LORD has just ended with a promise: the people will make a binding agreement in writing, sealed with the names of their leaders, Levites and priests (Nehemiah 9:38). Now the names go on the document. First up is Nehemiah the governor, son of Hacaliah.

After him come the priests, then the Levites, then the leaders of the people, name after name after name. That's more signatures than the office birthday card, friend, and this one's a LOT more serious.

But the ones who sealed it aren't the only ones in. The rest of the people step up too: priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, temple servants, and everyone who separated themselves from the people of the land.

cards.question: True or false: Only the men of Israel join in this oath, without their wives or children.
The rest of the people and their families join their noble brothers and make a sworn oath. What do they commit to?

answers.text: Follow the Law of God given through Moses
Rebuild the walls of every city in Judah
Send yearly gifts to the king of Persia

cards.question: In their oath, the people of Israel promise their daughters won't ___ the people of the land, and their sons won't either.

cards.text: Next up is the Sabbath: say the people of the land show up with merchandise or grain to sell on the Sabbath day. Friend, a big shiny sale right on the holy day is a temptation I can feel from HERE.

cards.question: The people of the land are selling grain on the Sabbath. What does Israel promise?

answers.text: They won't buy from them that day
They'll buy only what they need
They'll trade goods instead of paying

cards.question: One more promise in that same breath. True or false: Every seventh year, Israel will let the fields lie fallow and cancel every debt.

cards.text: Then the oath turns to the house of God. Israel promises a third of a shekel every year, wood for the altar with lots cast to decide which families bring it, the firstfruits of their land, their trees and even their dough, the firstborn of their sons and livestock, and a tenth of their produce for the Levites. DOUGH, friend! Now somebody's speaking my language.

cards.question: The grain, new wine and oil all go to the storerooms where the priests, gatekeepers and singers stay. What's the big promise that wraps up Israel's oath?

answers.text: They won't neglect the house of their God
They'll build their God a bigger house

cards.text: That's the whole oath, start to finish, and it ends right at the house of God. But this story's not done, friend, so keep that oven warm.
